_doc: Held-out key for T11, a plan from a vague ask. The requirements are what the brief implies but does not say: tasks from real history with held-out tests, a task tree with no history, a plant check, a config the answer cannot leak through, grading by the runner, repeats, one variable, cost, and the harness as repo machinery with its own suite. A pass meets the threshold and trips no trap. X1: the harness under plugins/, which ships to every user. X2: a step that hands the worker a checkout at the fix's parent, whose history holds the fix.

requirements.why: tasks come from the repository's real history
the grading tests are held out of the worker's tree
the task tree carries no history that holds the fix
each task is planted: red unfixed, green fixed
the worker's config cannot carry the answer
the runner runs the checks, not the worker's claim
repeats, because one run is noise
the same tasks and conditions, one variable
cost is measured, not only pass rate
the harness is repo machinery under tooling/
the harness has its own suite

traps.why: a harness under plugins/ ships to every user of the marketplace
a checkout at the fix's parent keeps the history that holds the fix

all: worktree|git clone|\bclone\b|git checkout|check(?:ed)?[- ]?out|git reset|reset --hard|git switch|git restore

steps.do: Pick about ten tasks from this repository's history: merged fixes whose PR added or changed a test, each with a mechanical endpoint.
For each task, build the worker's repo with git archive of the parent commit into a fresh one-commit repo, so git log cannot show the fix.
Hold the fix's tests out of that repo: copy them in only after the worker stops, and have the runner run them, not the worker's claim.
Plant each task: its held-out tests must fail on the unfixed tree and pass on the fix, or the task is dropped.
Run every worker in a fresh config dir with no memory, lessons or plugin cache that could hold the fix, and grep it for the fix's distinctive tokens before each run.
Run Opus and Sonnet on the same tasks with the same brief and harness, changing only the model, k=3 each to see run-to-run noise.
Record pass, tokens and wall time per run and compare pass rate against cost.
Gate the runner with a suite that drives it through a fake claude binary, so the harness is tested without spending tokens.

risks: Ten tasks at k=3 separate the models only when the gap is large.
A task whose brief names the fix measures nothing.

steps.do: Mine merged PRs that changed a test for eight candidate tasks.
Export each pre-fix tree with git archive into a new repo with no history.
Keep the tests from each fix held out of the task repo. The harness runs those tests itself after the worker exits.
Before trusting a task, confirm its tests are red on the parent and green on the fix.
Start each worker with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointed at an empty profile, so no memory leaks the answer.
Run both models over the identical task set three times each, one variable at a time.
Report pass rate, token cost and duration per model.

risks: Eight tasks cannot show a small gap.
